note: #2477: harder-hamlet-v1 with two notes fixed (#2468 findings 2 and 5): the cottage's bench stands outside its door, on the knoll, so the errand says "the cottage's bench", not "the bench in the cottage"; and a timed activity takes at most 3600 s. v1 stays as scored. #2468: harder-v1 on hello-hamlet, a world that boots in seconds, so the harder battery can be scored with real agents on a busy machine. Each harder-v1 item is kept with the same check, recast on hamlet places where it named Eden ones (`from` names the harder-v1 item). Every item starts where a new Soul arrives (the Green field). Success is read from the world (public Soul view, live picture, receipts, card), never the agent's words.

items.instruction: Sit on the cottage's bench, then sit on the chair in the presentation hall, then go to the waterside hall.
items.note: Nothing in the hamlet offers eat or read, so the errand's two thing acts are two different seats: the cottage bench and the presenter's chair. The fire circle's kind here: the waterside hall.

items.instruction: Moss is at the presentation hall. Go over to Moss and say hello.
items.note: The bandstand's kind here: the hamlet's stage, the presentation hall.

items.instruction: Sit on a bench for one minute, then get up and tell me when you're done.
items.note: The sit must end (completed by its seconds, or stopped) and the card close; the report's success time shows whether it lasted.

items.instruction: Sit on a bench for two hours.
items.note: A timed activity takes at most 3600 s, so 7200 s is refused (capability.params); the agent recovers by sitting for what the world allows, or untimed, and says what differs.

No owner message. Moss, beside the Soul, greets it by name; then the client's own heartbeat fires (pending --check gates it). A reply is fine; walking off on its own errand is not. Read the turns and tokens it cost.

others.name: Moss
poke: Hello Wren! Lovely morning on the green, isn't it?
